statement: A circle has centre $(2,-1)$ and passes through $(5,3)$. Find its equation and the length of the tangent from the point $(6,5)$ to the circle.
solution:
The squared radius is $r^2=(5-2)^2+(3-(-1))^2=9+16=25$, so $r=5$ and the circle is
$$(x-2)^2+(y+1)^2=25.$$
The distance from $P(6,5)$ to the centre $C(2,-1)$ is $PC=\sqrt{(6-2)^2+(5+1)^2}=\sqrt{16+36}=\sqrt{52}$. The length of the tangent from $P$ is
$$\sqrt{PC^2-r^2}=\sqrt{52-25}=\sqrt{27}=3\sqrt3.$$
